@@U02393@@
Good, but don’t stop there;
describe him precisely.

@@U02395@@
How does one describe dignity?
That healthy moon of a face
and full mouth,
the full-blown cheeks
beneath a handsome turban,
and luxuriously comfortable
in his pleated robe!
And what’s to be said
of his noble bearing!
He looks every inch the ruler!

@@U02397@@
He’s 普路托斯,
god of Wealth,
come in splendor
to your Emperor
who desires mightily
to see him.

@@U02399@@
And you?
Tell us of yourself.
Who are you?

@@U02401@@
I am Prodigality.
I am Poetry.
The spendthrift who achieves fulfillment
by squandering what is most personal to him.
Like 普路托斯, I am immeasurably rich;
I enliven his dances,
his feasts and festivals,
and what he lacks I supply.
translation:
@@U02393@@
很好，但不要就此止步；
准确地描述他。

@@U02395@@
怎样形容一个人的尊严呢？
那张健康的月亮脸
和满嘴，
饱满的脸颊
帅气的头巾下，
和奢华舒适
穿着他的百褶长袍！
以及要说的话
体现了他的高贵气质！
他看起来浑身都是统治者！

@@U02397@@
他是普路托斯，
财神爷，
光彩夺目
给你的皇帝
谁强烈渴望
去看他。

@@U02399@@
你呢？
告诉我们你自己吧。
你是谁？

@@U02401@@
我是挥霍者。
我是诗。
挥霍者获得满足
浪费对他来说最私人的东西。
像普路托斯一样，我非常富有；
我让他的舞蹈充满活力，
他的节期和节日，
他所缺乏的，我来供给。
